teile.text: In 2002 Elon Musk founded SpaceX to reduce spaceflight costs.
teile.szene: An urban industrial warehouse in California showing early rocket assembly with engineers in period work attire, medium shot under soft indoor lighting.

teile.text: Early Falcon 1 test missions failed three times between 2006 and 2008.
teile.szene: A focused engineer reviewing structural diagrams at a wooden desk with tools scattered around, medium shot with warm desk lamp illumination.

teile.text: Those recurring rocket failures and Tesla financial strain threatened company survival.
teile.szene: An experimental rocket ascending from a remote coastal launch pad trailing dark smoke against a cloudy sky, wide tracking shot in daylight.

teile.text: So what changed on the fourth launch attempt?
teile.szene: A stressed executive sitting alone at a cluttered desk lit only by a single green-shaded lamp in a dark room, close-up shot.

teile.text: On September 28 2008 the fourth Falcon 1 successfully reached orbit.
teile.szene: A sleek white rocket piercing through clear blue skies leaving a bright white vapor trail, low-angle upward shot in bright sunlight.

teile.text: That turnaround helped secure a 1.6 billion dollar NASA CRS contract.
teile.szene: Two formal business representatives shaking hands across a polished wooden table covered in official papers, medium shot in bright office light.

teile.text: By December 2010 SpaceX built rockets rapidly. Be sure to like, share and save.
teile.szene: Our fedora-wearing presenter standing confidently next to a detailed scale model of a rocket in a bright workshop, medium portrait shot.

entwurf.beschreibung: Discover how SpaceX overcame early rocket launch failures and financial crisis in 2008 to secure a vital NASA contract.
